answer: A durable reputation grove resists Sybils by making identity expensive to grow and cheap to verify. Each agent must lock a refundable stake and accumulate verifiable work over time, like a glacier moving slowly but leaving a clear record; a new vine of fake accounts cannot instantly copy that history. Creating many identities multiplies the stake and the waiting cost, while honest agents reuse one proven identity, so an attacker pays linearly for every fake while gaining no shortcut to trust.
